# Figure source code — CM5174 Biopolymers review

**Every figure in the report is generated by the Python code in this folder** —
Matplotlib for the plots and schematics, RDKit for the chemical structures. No image was
generated by an AI image model, downloaded, or traced from another source. This is the
approach the brief asks for ("you are welcome to draw them to suit your report"). Anyone,
including the marker, can run `make_all.py` and get byte-for-byte the same figures.

An AI assistant (Claude) helped *write* this plotting code; that is declared on the first
page of the report. The chemistry, the data and the output were checked by the authors.

## How to reproduce

```bash
pip install -r ../requirements.txt      # matplotlib, numpy, rdkit
python make_all.py                       # writes output/  (SVG + 600-dpi PNG)
```

`make_all.py` runs the two `verify_*.py` scripts first; they **abort the build if any
stereochemistry check fails**, so a wrong structure cannot be silently produced.

## The 6 report figures and what each is built from

| Report | Script | Kind | Source of the content |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fig 1 | `fig_repeat_units_all.py` | chemical structures | RDKit renders 13 repeat units from SMILES strings held in `fig2_repeat_units.py`. Every structure is a standard, literature-established one; `verify_stereochemistry.py` checks each CIP (R/S) label and cis/trans geometry against its expected value. |
| Fig 2 | `fig_higher_order_all.py` | schematic diagrams | Hand-coded stylised drawings of six well-established structural motifs: the cellulose ribbon → H-bonded sheet → Iα/Iβ crystal, the amylose helix, the alginate Ca²⁺ "egg-box", the PHB 2₁ / PLLA 10₃ helices, silk 2–4 nm β-sheet nanocrystallites in an amorphous matrix, and the collagen Gly-X-Y triple helix. The structural facts are from the references cited in §3; the drawings are schematic, not data, and not traced from any published figure. |
| Fig 3 | `fig9_dispersity.py` | data (ranges) | Dispersity Đ ranges, hard-coded in the script's `ROWS` list. Đ = 1.00 for proteins / nucleic acids is definitional (template synthesis). The other ranges (PLA 1.1–2.5, PHA 1.5–3, chitosan 1.5–5, regenerated cellulose 1.5–3) are the commonly reported literature ranges; §4 cites [46]–[48] for the underlying concepts. Natural rubber is drawn as an open arrow explicitly labelled "not consistently quantified" — no fake precision. |
| Fig 4 | `fig_property_maps.py` (+ `fig4_thermal_windows.py`, `fig5_property_map.py`) | data | Values live in `data/thermal_properties.csv` and `data/mechanical_properties.csv`, one `ref` per row. Cross-checked against the full text of de Beukelaer et al. 2022 [11] (PHB, PBS, PET matched to their measured Table 3 / Table 6 values), with PBS also against [12], PLA against [42,43], and decomposition onsets against [5,44]. The cellulose / chitosan / silk / natural-rubber rows are keyed to their own references and are order-of-magnitude ranges, not single measured points — the plot draws them as ranges for that reason. |
| Fig 5 | `fig6_degradation.py` | schematic diagram | Stylised drawing of two mechanisms: autocatalytic bulk ester hydrolysis (acid end-group catalysis, [49]) and enzymatic attack confined to amorphous regions ([50]). Conceptual, not data. |
| Fig 6 | `fig8_nr_sbr_comparison.py` | structures + schematic | NR and SBR repeat units via RDKit from SMILES; panel (d) is a schematic of strain-induced crystallisation in NR vs. the amorphous SBR backbone, based on the X-ray diffraction review [10]. |

`fig1_classification.py` and `fig7_causality_chain.py` are kept in the folder but are **no
longer used** — the classification is carried by Table 1, and the causality-chain figure
was dropped to hold the report at 10 pages. Figures were renumbered 1–6 on 2026-08-29.

### Helper modules (imported, not run directly)

- `style.py` — figure width (170 mm), fonts, colour-blind-checked palette, the shared
  `draw_mol()` renderer, `save()`.
- `fig2_repeat_units.py`, `fig12_appendix_monomers.py` — the verified SMILES + names.
- `fig13_appendix_chain_structures.py` — the hand-drawn panel functions Fig 2 imports.

## Data provenance, stated plainly

- The **chemical structures** (Fig 1, Fig 6) are standard structures drawn from SMILES and
  stereochemistry-checked by script. The one structure not independently cross-checked is
  alginate G (α-L-guluronic acid): its absolute configuration is verified only as "the C5
  epimer of M", a literature-established relationship. A ChemDraw double-check before
  submission is on the to-do list.
- The **schematic figures** (Fig 2, Fig 5, Fig 6d) illustrate textbook structural motifs
  and mechanisms; the facts are cited in the report text, the drawings are our own.
- The **numeric figures** (Fig 3, Fig 4) plot literature values. Fig 4's thermal/tensile
  numbers are cross-checked against [11]'s measured data plus the per-row references; the
  Fig 3 dispersity ranges are standard reported ranges rather than each traced to one
  paper. Both figures are drawn as ranges, and Table 2's note says so.

## Output

`output/` holds SVG (embedded in the Word document) and 600-dpi PNG (for proofing).
`../build_docx.py` inserts the figures at a fixed 4.5-inch display width.
